title: Genuine question, how to openly phrase "Built with AI tools, or it wouldnt have been built at all." Sort of disclaimer.
author: Chacudno
selftext:
I want to find a way to say what I believe which is "this game would not have been made without the use of AI tools, it's the only way I was ever going to get it done."

But I want to say it in better words. Words that are clear and direct but professional.

comments.author: Opening-West-4369
comments.body: how about saying nothing

comments.author: TemporalBias
comments.body:
The more you try to justify it, the less useful that justification becomes when the people you are trying to convince do not care about your justification. They only care that you used AI or not.

In other words, I myself will be saying something along these lines when I release my own AI-developed game: "I worked with AI to make this. If you don't like that, don't play the game."

replies.author: Chacudno
replies.body: Im not at all trying to justify, I just want a way to be upfront and direct as a way to clearly state my position.

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
Thats the trap you're falling into.  You feel a need to "state your position."  By doing so you're *inviting* them to act up.

Make the minimum required disclosure, period.  Anything beyond that only accomplishes inviting trouble.  Your game's product page is not the place to fight a holy war.

comments.author: fissionchips303
comments.body:
I would call out the actual tools used as a sort of special thanks, like:

AI Notice: This game was developed with the use of \_\_\_\_, \_\_\_\_, \_\_\_\_, \_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_\_. While we at <game company name> highly value artistic freedom and do not believe in using AI that would infringe on original creative works, we are also honored and grateful to the developers of these systems which have enabled us to create the game you are now playing. We have approached the use of AI with judiciousness, using it when appropriate and doing our best to balance our use of modern tools with a classic approach to craft. Without AI tools, this game would not have been built at all. We hope you enjoy our game.

comments.author: Adjective_Noun_67
comments.body:
Here's my lukewarm take:

The people most loudly demanding AI disclosure won't be satisfied with *any* explanation. They're on a witchhunt and want you to do the hard work for them by self-identifying as a valid target for their hate.

People who understand nuance are perceptive enough to tell if and how AI was used without you telling them, and unless it's used so heavily and implemented so poorly that it degrades the overall quality of the work, they won't care.

It's laughably ironic that the crowd parroting "all AI use is slop" are completely unable to tell when it's being used unless you spell it out for them, which just makes them angrier at their own incompetence. I don't owe those assholes transparency and neither do you.

comments.author: work_in_marketing
comments.body:
It's an interesting question and it's unfortunate how many of the comments here are kinda a mirror of the anti ai crowd instead of interacting with the question. Using ai to write code is becoming normalised so I assume your question is mostly about art and sound.

The common way I've seen other companies do it for boardgames is to phrase it something like "AI was used in the prototyping phase of the development". In theory it would leave the door open for as much ai as you want, as long as you afterwards touched the assets manually. The downside is that it probably won't satisfy people. Either you used ai and you're bad or they demand to see the exact usage so they can deem if it's acceptable from their personal scale.

The comment "Made possible with AI" sounds well but doesn't really answer anything and people might even get the impression that you one prompted the whole project which lowers the value of your work.

I'd say one downside of the hate is that it kinda removes the incitement to hire people. I'm planning on hire someone for voice lines and someone to do the UI - both far cheaper than people would assume. However, I'm still using ai for the 3d models so I'll get backlash regardless which kinda lowers my interest in outsourcing it.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
It depends on the circumstances. If your game is just a hobby project that you are not charging for then you don't need to mention it at all imo. If your game is good it won't look like it's made with AI anyway and if it isn't then the AI use will likely be obvious.

If you are charging people money then it's different. For example if something is heavily vibe coded it's probably going to put me off paying for it as there's a high chance the dev does not know what they are doing or even how their own game works. That means there's potentially going to be bugs, poor performance and general jank.

The same goes for art and assets, I would want to know if most of the assets are AI gen because it means they are likely going to be poor quality.

If you are asking for money from people it's always best to be upfront as it will just come back to bite you in the ass. 

Really there's two descriptions I would use, either:

"AI assisted" if your game is mostly hand made.

"AI generated content" if you have a lot of stuff that was mostly AI. Then a list of what.

Basically similar to how Steam requires.

It's understandable people don't want to mention AI use because of the hate, but when you're selling something people absolutely want to know and should know because it's something that can affect the end product in numerous negative ways.
